name: Aram
overview: Aram is identified in Scripture as both a person and a region connected to the descendants of Shem. Genesis 10:22-23 traces Aram as a son of Shem and lists his children, highlighting the familial lineage from which the Aramean people arose. Additionally, Genesis 22:21 names Aram as the son of Kemuel, further establishing his place in the genealogical record. Geographically, Aram refers to a region north of Canaan, known as the homeland of Balaam, whom Balak king of Moab summoned to curse Israel, as described in Numbers 23:7. These references together show Aram’s significance in biblical history both as an ancestral figure and a territory influencing Israel’s narrative.
